To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned the DB58 cDNA from D. biflores stems and leaves and that the deduced polypeptide is a single precursor to the two DB58 subunits.
we have cloned the cDNA encoding DB58, a leguminous lectin, and that it encodes a precursor protein that can be processed in vitro to generate the two subunits of DB58.
1) the DB58 lectins from Dolichos stem and leaves have been isolated, purified, and characterized; and 2) the DB58 mRNA has been cloned, and its primary structure determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a plant lectin that is found in the leaves and stems of the D. biflora plant.
the characterization of the biosynthesis, structure and function of the D. biflora lectin.
the characterization of a new lectin, DB58, from the stems and leaves of D. bifloris.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DB58 lectins from D. biflors are encoded by a single gene that is differentially expressed in the stems and leaves of D. biflorous plants.
the Dolichus biflorus seed and DB58 lectins are encoded for by different genes, and that the genes are differentially expressed.
the DB58 lectins are encoded in the mRNA of Dolichos biflora and that these lectins have been isolated from the leaves and stems of the plant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DB58 lectins from D. biflora stem and leaf tissue are encoded by a single polypeptid precursor that is post-translationally processed into two closely related subunit polypeptides.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown how a plant can have a single lectin gene that encodes two lectins that have different functions.
